name: Magdalena Bay
label: Mom + Pop
lede: Two Miami prog-rock kids swapped Rush for Grimes, taught themselves pop off YouTube, and ended up with a concept album about a girl whose brain rejects a CD.

eras.title: Prog kids in Miami
eras.text: Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin meet as teenagers in a North Miami music program and make progressive rock together. A winter break in 2016 turns them toward pop, a genre both had avoided.

q: We've been influencing each other's music taste since we were 15 years old.
years.src: Miami New Times · Gorilla vs. Bear · PAPER · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay
years.h: Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin meet in a classic rock cover band
years.p: Both are in high school when the Live! Modern School of Music, an after-school program in North Miami, puts them in the same cover band. They stay a duo for the next fifteen years.
years.xp:
The cover band did not last, but the pairing did: they formed the prog band Tabula Rasa with other musicians, including drummer [[Nick Villa|dbedcb83-60c1-4daa-9c4e-1b232b082866]], and made a self-titled EP, a self-titled album and a last record called Crimson. Tenenbaum told Gorilla vs. Bear the project was "pretty niche like progressive rock," with an audience mostly in Scandinavia.

Lewin told PAPER the pair have been swapping taste since they were teenagers, which is how a prog band ends up writing synth-pop.

years.src: Miami New Times · Gorilla vs. Bear · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Winter break: Tabula Rasa is over, Magdalena Bay is a pop duo
years.p: With Tenenbaum at Penn and Lewin at Northeastern, the two reconnect over Grimes and Carly Rae Jepsen and start writing pop by file transfer. The name comes from Maggie Bay, an administrator at Lewin's old job.
years.xp: Their first single, "Voc Pop," came out June 1, 2016 and has since been pulled from streaming. A cover of Tears for Fears' "Head over Heels" followed in September, shot on an old VHS camcorder: Tenenbaum told Miami New Times it was the first time they did the whole '80s retro thing, helped along by Miami's palm trees and neon.

eras.title: Los Angeles and a YouTube habit
eras.text: After moving to Los Angeles in 2018 the duo start releasing short videos and singles on a steady drip, and a small label bites. By 2020 they have an EP and a look: lo-fi VHS, pastel CGI.

years.cap: A Mag Minis episode. Image to be supplied.
years.src: Miami New Times · PAPER · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Mag Minis: a new short video every few weeks, made at home
years.p: The series starts in February 2019 with "Afternoon in Heaven." The clips are what make Luminelle Recordings sign the pair.
years.xp:
Lewin told Miami New Times the idea behind the mini-videos was to keep a steady flow of content after the move to Los Angeles in 2018. The pair edit the videos and do the visual effects themselves, a habit that runs through every later release.

The first batch was compiled as Mini Mix Vol. 1 on July 19, 2019. Day/Pop and Night/Pop, collecting remastered singles and covers, had come out the month before the series began.

years.src: Miami New Times · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: A Little Rhythm and a Wicked Feeling, the first proper EP
years.p: Eight tracks, released March 13, 2020 on Luminelle Recordings, about four months after the Mag Minis compilation.

eras.title: Mercurial World
eras.text: A debut album with its own website and video game turns into a fancam hit and a run supporting the biggest names in alt-pop. By 2023 they are at Coachella.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mercurial World · Gorilla vs. Bear · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Mercurial World lands, with a Y2K website and an 8-bit game
years.p: Two years of home recording, released October 8, 2021 on Luminelle. Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and Metacritic averaged 78.
years.xp:
The singles came in order: "Chaeri" June 30, "Secrets (Your Fire)" August 11, "You Lose!" September 15 and "Hysterical Us" October 5. Tenenbaum designed the Y2K-style promo website, and "You Lose!" got an 8-bit video game to go with its video.

"We just like making it as immersive as possible for however many people want to get lost in the sauce," Tenenbaum told Gorilla vs. Bear.

years.p: The Mercurial World track spreads after people start using it to soundtrack fancam edits, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mercurial World · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Opening for Charli XCX, then Primavera Sound
years.p: The duo support [[Charli XCX|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]] on her Crash tour, play Primavera Sound in June and Porter Robinson's Second Sky festival in October.
years.xp: A deluxe Mercurial World followed September 23, 2022: 28 tracks, remixes by Danny L Harle and Cecile Believe, and fan-recorded voicemails dubbed "secrets." Drummer Nick Villa, who had played on the album sessions since 2021, became a permanent live member that year.

years.h: Coachella in April, Lollapalooza in August, and three tours as openers
years.p: Between the two festivals they open for [[Caroline Polachek|d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a]] on her Spiraling Tour and [[Rina Sawayama|52494f9b-789d-4467-bcaf-9915e70cc8f6]] on Hold the Girl Reloaded.

eras.title: A disk, a demon hand, a No. 19
eras.text: Signed to Mom + Pop, the duo spend two years writing a loose sci-fi concept record, and Pitchfork ranks it among the year's best.

years.cap: Still from the Amanda Kramer video. Image to be supplied.
years.src: Wikipedia: Death & Romance · Wikipedia: Imaginal Disk
years.h: Mom + Pop, and a five-minute lead single called "Death & Romance"
years.p: The first release under the new deal is written in a two-week burst. Amanda Kramer directs the sci-fi video, which Tenenbaum stars in as True, and it opens the world of the album.
years.xp: The track came out May 28, 2024; the video, about three minutes longer than the song, followed June 18 and ends by teasing "Fear, Sex," the next track on the record. Paste later named it the best song of 2024, and it landed on Dork (#16), Stereogum (#32) and Pitchfork (#45) year-end lists. [[Dave Fridmann|6b09687f-72de-4337-9a0b-da8f6248ce7c]] mixed it.

q: I was thinking a lot about psychoanalysis and reading Solaris.
years.h: A girl named True, an implant, and a paperback
years.p: Tenenbaum says the concept grew from what she was reading while the band toured. The album follows True, who gets a disk meant to build her ideal self, and whose body rejects it.
years.xp: The title borrows from the imaginal discs in insect larvae that grow into adult body parts. The cover, made with artist Maria Shatalova, shows a demon hand pushing a CD into Tenenbaum's forehead. Lewin told PAPER they leave the lyrics open-ended so listeners can put their own meaning on them.

years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Imaginal Disk
years.h: Imaginal Disk: Pitchfork gave it 7.7 and ranked it No. 19 of 2024
years.p: Anna Gaca's review called it "musically and conceptually dense" for bending pop's optimism toward a more paranoid world. Metacritic averaged 85.
years.xp:
The singles were "Death & Romance" (May 28), "Image" (July 10), "Tunnel Vision" (July 31) and "That's My Floor" (August 21), all with Kramer videos. Drums were cut at the Honeymoon Suite in Los Angeles and orchestral parts in Stockholm; Justin Raisen added production on "Love Is Everywhere."

Outside Pitchfork's No. 19, NME and Stereogum both put the record at No. 5 for 2024, and Slant had it at No. 10. The Guardian and NME reviews each scored it full marks on Album of the Year's scale.

years.h: Late-night debut on Jimmy Kimmel Live!
years.p: The duo play "Image" for their late-night TV debut, a day after a remix of it by [[Grimes|7e5a2a59-6d9f-4a17-b7c2-e1eedb7bd222]] comes out.

eras.title: Second sleep
eras.text: The Imaginal Disk cycle runs into arena tours and a run of double singles, then a film.

yt: Ashes to Ashes (triple j Like A Version)
years.h: Covering David Bowie's "Ashes to Ashes" on Triple J
years.p: The duo play a sparkly version for Australia's Like a Version series, and follow it with "Image."

years.h: Big stages: support slots with Billie Eilish and Halsey
years.p: They open for [[Billie Eilish|f4abc0b5-3f7a-4eff-8f78-ac078dbce533]] on the Hit Me Hard and Soft tour and for [[Halsey|3377f3bb-60fc-4403-aea9-7e800612e060]] on For My Last Trick, and play Lollapalooza on July 31.

years.h: Four double singles and a box set called Nice Day
years.p: "Second Sleep" and "Star Eyes" lead off in September, then pairs in October and November, collected as Nice Day: A Collection of Singles. Wikipedia calls the run a spiritual successor to Imaginal Disk.
The visual album movie, announced August 23, 2025, debuts at the Tribeca Festival. A public release has not been announced.
